title: Healthier Salt Could Save Millions of Lives
paragraphs: Replacing regular salt with salt that has been enriched with potassium could save millions of lives, according to a new study. And most people won't notice a difference in taste.

An international team of researchers modeled the possible health benefits of changing to potassium-enriched salt across 193 countries, and found that a worldwide replacement of all salt would prevent almost 3 million deaths and over 10 million new cases of cardiovascular disease and kidney disease.

The salt that we use to flavor our food contains sodium — an essential nutrient. However, excessive sodium consumption causes high blood pressure, which increases the risk of kidney disease and cardiovascular disease.

Although the World Health Organization recommends people eat no more than 2 grams of sodium a day, the global average consumption is more than double that amount. And getting people to eat less salt is difficult — because they miss that salty taste!
However, switching to potassium-enriched salt both lowers sodium consumption and increases potassium intake — something the average person doesn't get enough of in their diet.
It's also commonly available at supermarkets and tastes about the same as regular salt.

In their study, the research team modeled several scenarios for replacing regular salt. In addition to replacing all salt worldwide, they looked at what would happen if only household salt was replaced, or if only the salt used in processed foods and restaurants was replaced.

They estimated that replacing just household salt would save almost 1.9 million lives and prevent over 6 million cases of cardiovascular disease and kidney disease. And replacing salt in processed foods and restaurants would save around 1.6 million lives and prevent over 5 million cases.
The study authors note that for some people who have advanced kidney disease, an increase in potassium could have negative health effects — so they should avoid potassium-enriched salt.
But for most people, the health benefits of salt replacement are clear, they said — and replacing salt is much cheaper than drug-based blood pressure treatments.
